document.title: Deck Apps play sounds on the desktop and the Vita
document.summary: Deck Apps declare `sounds` like images and play them with `playSound` and `stopSound`, through a vendored miniaudio `dev-0.12` on the host and the Vita, and the demo gets a Sound section.
document.why: Máté asked that [the SDK can play audio files from assets](source:s2), with a demo section, using miniaudio if it works on the PS Vita.

sources.label: PR #147
sources.title: feat(sdk): Deck Apps play sounds on the desktop and the Vita
sources.gist: Sounds declared in vitadeck.config.json, played by name on host and Vita via miniaudio dev-0.12; demo Sound section; host PipeWire capture as proof.

sources.label: Claude Code session · Nov 4
sources.gist: Add audio support so the SDK can play audio files from assets, add a demo section, use miniaudio.h after checking PS Vita support.

lookFor: The request asks for [miniaudio.h, checked for PS Vita support](source:s2). Released miniaudio has no Vita backend, so `vendor/miniaudio` is a submodule pinned to the unreleased `dev-0.12` branch, not a released single header; ADR 0006 gives the reason.

groups.title: miniaudio dev-0.12 as a submodule and its own library
groups.why: Only miniaudio's `dev-0.12` branch has a Vita backend, which the [request](source:s2) needs.
groups.summary: `.gitmodules` adds the shallow `vendor/miniaudio` submodule, and `CMakeLists.txt` builds it as a `-w` static library linked next to `vitadeck_core`, with the docs recording the pin.

attention.note: The pin `245bbb8` sits on an unreleased branch, so its API and Vita backend can change under a future bump. In exchange VitaDeck ships no audio code of its own under `src/platform/`. ADR 0006 says to move to a 0.12 release and retest on the Vita when the pin moves.

fileNotes.CMakeLists.txt: Submodule auto-init loop, `miniaudio` library, new sources and link order.
fileNotes.docs/adr/0006-miniaudio-dev-branch-for-s: New ADR: why dev-0.12, threading model, considered options.

groups.title: `sounds` in the package contract, C and TypeScript
groups.why: Footgun 2 in AGENTS.md: the manifest is produced by the CLI and validated natively, so both sides learn `sounds` together.
groups.summary: The CLI copies `sounds` to `sounds/` and types their names in `sound-names.d.ts`, and `package_manifest.c` accepts the same field, each through one shared asset routine instead of per-kind copies.

attention.note: `schemaVersion` stays 1 although the manifest gains `sounds`. An older host skips the unknown key and loads the package, but `playSound` is then missing from its runtime SDK and throws. A package without sounds is byte-for-byte the same shape as before.

fileNotes.tests/package_manifest_harness.c: Accepts sounds; rejects bad name, `.ogg`, missing file.

groups.title: Sound registry and the native play and stop functions
groups.why: Playback itself: the registry loads a package's sounds with the asset reload and the JS thread plays them by name.
groups.summary: `bootstrap.c` calls `sound_registry_load_package` beside the font and image registries, and `jslib/sound.c` exposes `nativePlaySound` and `nativeStopSound` over the registry in `src/audio/sounds.c`.

attention.note: The JS thread reads `g_package_sounds` without a lock. That is safe only because `src/main.c` stops the JS thread before `bootstrap_reload_active_package_fonts`, the one caller that rewrites the registry. A future caller that reloads assets with the JS thread running would race.

fileNotes.src/audio/sounds.h: Registry API and its JS-thread-stopped rule.
fileNotes.src/jslib/sound.c: Throws `RangeError` for an undeclared sound name.
fileNotes.src/core/bootstrap.c: Loads, clears on failure, and shuts down the sound registry.
fileNotes.js/packages/runtime/src/runtime-native.d: Declares the two native globals for the runtime.

groups.title: `playSound` and `stopSound` in the SDK
groups.why: The author-facing surface the [request](source:s2) names: the SDK plays audio files from assets.
groups.summary: `sound.ts` wraps the native functions with `SoundName`-typed `playSound(name, { loop })` and `stopSound(name)`, which `index.tsx` exports and the docs describe.

fileNotes.js/packages/sdk/src/index.tsx: Exports them and the sound types.
fileNotes.js/packages/sdk/README.md: Config field, generated types, and a Sound section.
fileNotes.CONTEXT.md: Adds **Deck App Sound** and lists `sounds` in the manifests.

groups.title: Demo Sound section and the tests that count sections
groups.why: The [request](source:s2) asks for a demo section; inserting it fourth shifts every index the smoke test, input harness and benchmark rely on.
groups.summary: `SoundSection` plays the chime and toggles the MP3 loop, and inserting it after Image renumbers the smoke pages and goldens, adds an input-harness round and one `r` to `demo-scroll`.

attention.note: `demo-scroll` still measures the Scroll section, now with a 13-button nav list. The Vita3K and Vita baselines in `tests/bench/baselines/` were not re-recorded, so the next comparison against them includes that small extra render cost.

fileNotes.js/examples/demo/src/sections/SoundSecti: Chime button, loop toggle, loop stopped on unmount.
fileNotes.js/examples/demo/src/App.tsx: Adds the section; nav buttons shrink to 28 px to fit 13.
fileNotes.tests/fixtures/golden/Linux/04-sound.png: New golden for the Sound section.
fileNotes.tests/fixtures/golden/Linux/01-rect-them: Header shows `/13` and the extra nav row.
fileNotes.tests/fixtures/golden/Linux/05-button.pn: Renumbered golden, same header and nav change.

commits.subject: feat: Deck App Sounds with playSound and stopSound
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Deck Apps declare sounds (.wav, .mp3, .flac) in vitadeck.config.json like
images; the CLI copies them into the package and types their names, the
native manifest validates them, and src/audio plays them through
miniaudio on the host and the Vita. The demo gets a Sound section.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
